queries.query: "large language model" AND ("network configuration" OR NetOps OR "network management") AND (generate OR synthesis OR translation)
queries.rationale: Locate primary papers that apply LLMs to generate or translate network intents/configurations to identify observed failure modes and task formulations.

queries.query: "LLM" OR "large language model" AND (hallucinat* OR "misinformation" OR "incorrect output" OR misprediction) AND (network OR NetOps OR "configuration")
queries.rationale: Find literature documenting LLM factual errors and hallucinations in operational/networking contexts to characterize phenomenology.

queries.query: "generate-validate-repair" OR "validate-and-repair" OR "verify-and-repair" AND (LLM OR "large language model" OR "generative model")
queries.rationale: Survey architectures that combine generation, automated validation, and iterative repair — central mitigations for NetOps use-cases.

queries.query: "formal verification" AND ("network configuration" OR "network policy" OR reachability OR "loop freedom" OR "access control")
queries.rationale: Identify formal/deterministic validators used in NetOps to assess how they can be used as oracles for LLM output checking.

queries.query: "tool-assisted" OR "verifier-assisted" OR "checker-assisted" AND (LLM OR "agent") AND (NetOps OR "network configuration")
queries.rationale: Find work on tool-augmented LLM pipelines and how external verifiers are integrated into agentic workflows for operational tasks.

queries.query: "prompt sensitivity" OR "prompt robustness" AND (LLM OR "large language model") AND (network OR NetOps OR configuration)
queries.rationale: Assess how prompt formulation and small perturbations change NetOps outputs — informs experimental control and threats to construct validity.

queries.query: "LLM" AND (calibration OR "confidence estimation" OR "uncertainty") AND (validation OR "out-of-distribution")
queries.rationale: Locate methods to extract or calibrate model confidence for gating potentially dangerous NetOps actions.

queries.query: "agentic" OR "autonomous agent" AND (NetOps OR network OR operations) AND (safety OR reliability OR governance)
queries.rationale: Survey literature on agentic systems applied to operations and their proposed safety/governance controls relevant to NetOps automation.

queries.query: "AIOps" OR "ML for operations" OR "AI for IT operations" AND benchmark OR evaluation
queries.rationale: Find existing AIOps benchmarks and evaluation practices to judge their applicability and limitations for LLM-driven NetOps experiments.
source_preferences: IEEE, ACM, arXiv, industry benchmark repositories (GitHub)

queries.query: "NetOps benchmark" OR "network configuration benchmark" OR "networking dataset" AND (LLM OR evaluation)
queries.rationale: Identify task datasets/benchmarks (public) for intent-to-configuration, repair, or policy verification to reuse or critique.

queries.query: "Mininet" OR "ns-3" OR "GNS3" AND (evaluation OR emulation OR "network testbed") AND ("LLM" OR "automation")
queries.rationale: Discover simulators/emulators used to execute or validate generated configs and methods for mapping generated configs to runnable tests.

queries.query: "reachability verification" AND (Cisco OR Juniper OR "access control" OR ACL OR "policy compliance")
queries.rationale: Collect domain-specific validators and metrics (reachability, isolation, ACL equivalence) used to operationally assess correctness.

queries.query: "dataset contamination" OR "data leakage" OR "training data overlap" AND (LLM OR foundation model) AND (benchmark OR evaluation)
queries.rationale: Understand threats to external validity arising from benchmarks being in model training data — critical for honest evaluation of LLM NetOps capabilities.

queries.query: "human-in-the-loop" AND (NetOps OR network management) AND (LLM OR automation OR agent) AND (validation OR oversight)
queries.rationale: Survey human oversight patterns (gating, review, rollback) used in operational deployments and experiments to inform mitigations and evaluation design.

queries.query: "failure mode" OR "error analysis" AND (LLM OR "large language model") AND (automation OR agent OR decision-making)
queries.rationale: Gather general LLM failure-mode taxonomies (misalignment, brittleness, hallucination) applicable to NetOps to structure failure analysis.

queries.query: "LangChain" OR "AutoGPT" OR "ReAct" OR "tool-using agents" AND (evaluation OR safety)
queries.rationale: Investigate common orchestration frameworks used to build agentic workflows and known limitations when applied to operational tasks.

queries.query: "benchmarks" AND (validity OR "threats to validity" OR "evaluation pitfalls") AND (ML OR LLM OR "foundation models")
queries.rationale: Collect methodological critiques of benchmark design and interpretation to inform how to evaluate LLMs for NetOps responsibly.
source_preferences: meta-science/ML evaluation papers, arXiv, major ML conferences

inclusion_criteria: Primary sources: peer-reviewed publications, preprints (arXiv/tech reports) with reproducible artifacts or clear methods
Public datasets, code repositories, and benchmarks with public access and versioning
Works from 2016–2026, prioritized 2019–2026 for LLM relevance
Papers that include evaluation methodology, metrics, validators, or code for NetOps or related AIOps tasks
Formal-methods and networking-spec sources (IETF RFCs, vendor docs) when cited for validators or operational semantics
Industry technical reports only if they include reproducible artifacts or clear methodological detail
exclusion_criteria: Non-technical marketing blurbs, high-level blog posts without methods or reproducible artifacts (unless they point to code/reports)
Sources that cannot be retrieved or whose metadata cannot be verified
Papers outside the 2016–2026 window unless historical context is essential
Work that only tests generic NLP QA on networking trivia without operational evaluation or validation
Proprietary internal reports with no public artifact or verifiable methodology
date_rationale: Focus on 2016–2026 to capture the rise of deep-learning based network automation and the LLM era; emphasize 2019–2026 (transformer and foundation-model proliferation) while allowing earlier formal-methods/networking validators for foundational techniques.
